title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 164
paragraphs: As for the Phocaians, since the men of Chios would not sell them, at their request, the islands called Oinussai — fearing lest these islands might be made a seat of trade and their island might be shut out of it — they set out for Kyrnos. For in Kyrnos, twenty years before this, they had established a city named Alalia, in accordance with an oracle (Arganthonios was by then dead). When they were setting out for Kyrnos, they first sailed to Phocaia and slaughtered the Persian garrison, to whose charge Harpagos had delivered the city. After they had achieved this, they made solemn imprecations on any of their number who should stay behind from their voyage, and moreover they sank a mass of iron in the sea, swearing that not until that mass should appear again on the surface would they return to Phocaia. However, as they were setting forth to Kyrnos, more than half the citizens were seized with yearning and regret for their city and for their native land, and they proved false to their oath and sailed back to Phocaia. But those of them who kept the oath still weighed anchor from the islands of Oinussai and sailed on.
